acceptance: The 'Dispatch and implement' section carries a prompt of at most 12 lines that covers the six points in step 1, and every point matches a rule stated elsewhere in the same doc.
The outcome of the subagent commit trial is recorded on this item with the commands used: allowed as is, or the exact refusal and what it needed.
The skill-reload behaviour is recorded on this item with how it was observed, and the doc reflects it or the item says why not.
`make pr-preflight` passes and the change is merged to `develop` in a pull request that touches no file outside `docs/agent/`.
context:
2026-11-13 results.
Step 1: the prompt (nine lines, six points) is in the 'Dispatch and implement' section, pull request #4205.
Step 2, subagent commit trial: done in real use, not a simulation. The leader of registered batch `member-rule-docs` ran `make batch-member-create` for two members and dispatched each as a subagent of its own session with that prompt. Both subagents committed on their member branches in the leader-created worktrees (a929304196 and 713e0bc905, author Joe Harris from the pinned worktree identity) with absolute paths only. No worktree-ownership refusal, no takeover variable, no primary-clone hook refusal, no override.
Step 3, skill reload: in omp a skill is read from disk when the session opens `skill://<name>`, so a session that has not yet read the skill gets the current text, and one that already read it keeps the old text in its context until it reads again or restarts. Observed in the session that made the rule change: `skill://todo` resolved to `.claude/skills/todo/SKILL.md` in the primary clone. Other harnesses were not checked. The only page that describes skill loading is the 'Skills and generated mirrors' paragraph in `AGENTS.md`, which has 31 bytes of budget left, so the doc was not changed.
Side finding, not fixed here: the gitignored `.agents/skills/todo/SKILL.md` in the primary clone is dated 2026-10-01 and lacks the new rule; it is refreshed only by `make skill-sync` in that checkout, which agents may not run there.

2026-11-13, addition to the step 2 result. A subagent that writes in a worktree its parent created becomes that worktree's session owner. For the two batch members this needed nothing: the leader lands from the integration worktree and never writes in a member worktree, and both landings passed. For a non-batch worktree handed to a subagent it does matter: after the subagent finished, the parent's `make pr-open` there was refused with 'Worktree ... is owned by live session <subagent session> (pid ...); this session is <parent session>', and the parent had to run `BENCHBOX_WORKTREE_TAKEOVER=1 make agent-write-preflight` first. `docs/internal/dev-loop-worktrees.md` already documents this (subagents share the harness pid, so a finished subagent's claim never goes stale), but no page under `docs/agent/` or `AGENTS.md` links it. Whether `make batch-finish` needs the same takeover for member worktrees is recorded when the batch closes.

2026-11-13, batch close: `make batch-finish EXECUTE=1` removed both subagent-owned member worktrees and their branches and finished the integration worktree with no takeover and no override. So the whole registered-batch path works with subagent members as documented; the takeover is needed only when a parent wants to write in a non-batch worktree after its subagent did.
description:
Since 2026-11-12 `docs/agent/batch-feature-delivery.md` allows a batch member to run as a subagent of its leader, and requires the dispatch prompt to forbid tracker writes and to require absolute worktree paths. It gives no text to copy, so each leader words the prompt itself and may still stop to ask whether its wording is enough. Two assumptions behind the rule were also never tried.

Work.
1. Add a short dispatch prompt to the 'Dispatch and implement' section: make no tracker write of any kind; pass an absolute path under the member worktree to every file tool; implement only inside the frozen scope; run `make batch-member-check`; stop with the landing report (branch, accepted head, base, changed files, tests); open no pull request.
2. Try it: from one session, create a worktree and have a subagent make and commit a change in it using only absolute paths. Record whether the worktree ownership checks and the primary-clone write hook allow it.
3. Find out whether a session that was already running when a skill mirror changed keeps the old skill text until it restarts, and say so in one sentence where the doc tells leaders how skills are loaded, or record that no such place exists.

Decision gates.
- If step 2 needs an extra step or an override (for example a worktree takeover variable), stop before documenting it as normal: report it, because a rule that needs an override on every use will bring the owner question back.
- If the instruction-size budget for agent docs blocks the added text (see agent-instruction-budget-headroom), shorten the prompt; do not raise the budget in this item.

Guardrails.
- The doc is the batch protocol: deliver serially, never through a registered batch, and do not start a batch to test this.
- Step 2 uses an ordinary worktree and a throwaway branch that is deleted afterwards; nothing is pushed and no tracker write is made by the subagent.
- The prompt restates existing member rules only; it adds no new permission and removes none.
